articles.title: How Many Closed Findings Before You Trust a Routing Change
articles.excerpt: How Many Closed Findings Before You Trust a Routing Change This week X spent its energy arguing about whether a headline number is real. A vLLM post claims DeepSeek V4.1 Flash runs 58× the throughput…
articles.body: How Many Closed Findings Before You Trust a Routing Change This week X spent its energy arguing about whether a headline number is real. A vLLM post claims DeepSeek V4.1 Flash runs 58× the throughput of GB300 NVL72 on Vera Rubin hardware. The replies immediately asked how it was measured, and at what concurrency. Another post pointed out that DeepSeek's cheapest price is a caching artifact: input the model has already seen costs $0.003 per million tokens off-peak instead of $0.15 — fifty times less — so a "cheap" agent run may just be a well-cached one. A third thread argues over forensic evidence about what hardware trained the newest models at all. Nobody on that timeline is arguing about the models. They are arguing about the evidence.
articles.author: Alex Chen

articles.body: A wallet's invoicing Mini App works on a developer's current phone. Its new document-import flow calls a host capability introduced in the latest wallet build. An earlier wallet can still support manual draft creation, but it does not implement that handoff. Meanwhile, the provider's backend is preparing to accept the imported invoice items. The release decision concerns a set of running combinations. It cannot be reduced to whether the newest Mini App package passed its own tests. This illustrative integration uses a document-import capability implemented by the wallet team, with its own interface contract. Track the independently changing layers FinClip supplies the Mini App runtime SDK, development tools and management platform.

articles.title: A stop-loss decision tree for TikTok Shop GMV Max campaigns
articles.excerpt: A falling ROAS is not, by itself, a reason to pause a TikTok Shop campaign. The right decision depends on whether the change is temporary noise, incomplete attribution, creative fatigue, or a genuine…
articles.body: A falling ROAS is not, by itself, a reason to pause a TikTok Shop campaign. The right decision depends on whether the change is temporary noise, incomplete attribution, creative fatigue, or a genuine loss of unit economics. This decision tree keeps those cases separate. It is designed for operators who need a repeatable review at the end of each day without rebuilding yesterday's profit report. Start with completed economics, not dashboard revenue Use four values for the same attribution window: settled or estimated net revenue; product cost and fulfillment cost; platform and payment fees; ad spend and known refunds. Calculate contribution profit before making a campaign decision.

articles.body: This week we loaded a third-party Wazuh decoder and rules file, exactly as published, into a clean Wazuh 4.14.7 manager (the official wazuh/wazuh-manager:4.14.7 container). It had three separate problems. One stopped the manager. The other two left it running with rules that could never fire. None of the three is exotic, so we rebuilt each one with made-up names ( myapp ) and measured it again on its own. Everything below is from those reruns. The test line, a syslog line with a JSON body: Nov 10 10:30:00 web01 myapp: {"event":"deny","user":"alice","action":"block"} 1. <field name="action"> on a static field: the manager does not start action is one of Wazuh's static fields, like srcip or dstuser .

articles.title: Google Sheets now lets others explore your data without accessing your spreadsheet
articles.excerpt: Let your data do the talking, without revealing everything else.
articles.body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users publish Gemini-powered Canvas dashboards, calendars, and task boards through shareable links. People can interact with a published Canvas without accessing or editing the original spreadsheet. Users can control who sees the Canvas and choose whether it updates automatically when spreadsheet data changes. Google Sheets is great for organizing information, but sharing it with others isn’t always convenient. Say you’re managing a project with multiple deadlines and tasks. You might have everything organized in a spreadsheet, but no one wants to scroll through dozens of rows just to see what’s happening next. Google already has a feature called Canvas that uses Gemini to turn spreadsheet data into interactive dashboards, calendars, and task boards.

articles.body: SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan. articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.excerpt: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.body: A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered. When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices. Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

articles.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
articles.excerpt: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT…
articles.body: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China.
